analysis.title: BofA Securities Equity Client Flow Trends: Extreme outflows week
key_insights: Clients sold US equities in the week of 10/12-10/16 (S&P 500 -1.9%), led by record single stock outflows of -$14.8bn, the 25th largest when normalized by S&P 500 market cap. Clients bought equity ETFs (+$2.8bn) after selling the prior week.

All client groups sold US equities. Institutional clients led (3rd week of selling, 10th biggest selling week by this group since 2008). Retail sold after buying the prior 2 weeks. Hedge funds sold for the first time in 5 weeks.

October is typically the biggest net selling month for institutional clients because of mutual fund tax loss selling ahead of the 10/31 deadline. Institutional outflows month to date, normalized by market cap, are larger than any other October on record.

Corporate client buybacks accelerated for the 3rd week but are slightly below seasonal averages. Annualized YTD buybacks are tracking below 2024-25 levels but above 2010-23 annual levels. Rolling 52-week buybacks as a % of S&P 500 market cap are the lowest since Aug 2021.
Clients sold stocks in 8 of 11 sectors, led by Tech (2nd biggest outflow ever, 15th biggest when normalized by Tech market cap). Tech single stock outflow was -$9.1bn.

Industrials had record outflows (-$2.8bn) in its 12th week of outflows, the largest ever and 3rd largest as a % of Industrials market cap. Trailing 12-week flows as a % of market cap are at an all-time high.
Energy saw the largest inflows (+$163mn single stocks, first Energy inflow in 6 weeks). Clients also bought Real Estate and Staples stocks.
ETF flows were positive across all styles (Value/Blend/Growth) and size segments. Clients sold ETFs in 8 sectors, led by Tech (-$116mn). Health Care ETFs saw the largest inflows (+$152mn).
Institutional single stock selling was -$8.0bn last week, with Tech at -$6.5bn and Industrials at -$2.3bn. Institutional ex-broker-dealer clients were the biggest net sellers (-$7.2bn).
Large cap single stocks saw -$10.3bn of net selling last week. Total net flows across stocks and equity ETFs were -$9.1bn, versus a 4-week average of -$4.4bn and a 52-week average of -$0.7bn.
The rolling 4-week average of US equity flows (stocks plus ETFs) is -$6.0bn.
YTD 2026 single stock flows are -$94.6bn, with institutional clients at -$64.0bn and private clients at -$48.5bn. Hedge funds are +$18.0bn. Equity ETF flows YTD are +$60.8bn.

Corporate buybacks YTD are $86.5bn. Rolling 52-week buybacks are 0.18% of S&P 500 market cap, down from a peak of 0.42% in Feb 2025. The last 12 weeks of buybacks were highest in Financials ($7.1bn) and Tech ($3.9bn).

Sector flow z-scores for the latest week are lowest in Technology (-2.43 vs 3 months, -5.57 vs 5 years) and Industrials (-1.44 vs 3 months, -4.52 vs 5 years). Energy is the highest at +1.33 vs 3 months.

sector_views.rationale: Client flow data only. Tech saw the 2nd biggest single stock outflow ever (-$9.1bn) and Tech ETFs also saw outflows. This describes flows, not a BofA rating.
Client flow data only. Record outflows of -$2.8bn in the 12th straight week of selling, with trailing 12-week flows relative to market cap at an all-time high.
Client flow data only. Largest sector inflow last week and the first Energy inflow in 6 weeks, though the rolling 4-week average is still negative.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Equity index fell as clients sold US single stocks at a record pace.

risk_factors: Weekly flow data can be influenced by block trades and is more volatile than the 4-week average.
Corporate buyback support is weak: rolling 52-week buybacks as a % of S&P 500 market cap are the lowest since Aug 2021.
Tax loss selling by mutual funds ahead of the 10/31 deadline may keep institutional selling elevated through the end of October.

Exhibit 21: rolling 52-week corporate client buybacks as a % of S&P 500 market cap peaked at 0.42% in Feb 2025 and are currently 0.18%, the lowest since 2021.
Exhibit 20: corporate client buybacks over the last 12 weeks have been highest in Financials ($7.1bn) and Tech ($3.9bn).
vol_and_positioning: Client net flows into US equities (stocks plus equity ETFs) were -$9.1bn last week against a 4-week average of -$4.4bn.

Institutional clients have sold for 3 straight weeks. Their month to date October outflows relative to market cap are the largest of any October on record, driven partly by tax loss selling before the 10/31 mutual fund deadline.
Hedge fund clients sold single stocks (-$1.8bn) for the first time in 5 weeks but remain net buyers over the past 12 months. They bought equity ETFs (+$0.9bn).
Private clients sold single stocks (-$2.1bn) and bought equity ETFs (+$0.9bn).

Rolling 4-week average single stock outflows are in their 4th straight week for institutional clients and large caps. Small caps flipped to outflows for the first time since late June, and mid cap net flows flipped negative.
Clients have been selling single stocks (-$94.6bn YTD) and buying equity ETFs (+$60.8bn YTD) this year.
